summary.name: Visual Studio Code
summary.one_liner: Visual Studio Code is Microsoft's free, open-source code editor that adds AI agent collaboration, debugging, and extensions for writing and managing code.
use_cases: write and debug code in one editor
review and steer AI agent code edits
run parallel agent tasks across repositories
develop over SSH or in WSL
summary.what_it_does: The page describes VS Code as an editor for writing, debugging, testing, and refactoring code, with language support, navigation, and integrated debuggers. It includes agent features: agents that work from a plan, make edits in the editor, and let users review results, plus an Agents window for coordinating multiple agents across repositories. Users can pick models from Anthropic, OpenAI, Google, Microsoft, and open-weight providers, or bring their own key, and use Copilot, Claude, or Codex as the agent harness. Remote options include containers, SSH, WSL, Dev Tunnels, and vscode.dev in the browser, and the Visual Studio Marketplace offers extensions.
notable: Open-source editor with public roadmap and issues
Supports multiple AI models and agent harnesses (Copilot, Claude, Codex) including BYOK
Remote development via containers, SSH, WSL, and browser at vscode.dev
Extensions from the Visual Studio Marketplace
caveats: Agent features depend on model and harness choices; the page does not state pricing for these
